goal.statement: Build a real-time Black-Scholes options pricing pipeline on Tradier + Spark Structured Streaming
goal.terminal_capability: Stream a Tradier option chain, price every contract with Black-Scholes, and account for where the model diverges from the market

nodes.title: What an option contract is
nodes.why: Every row in your stream is one contract. Without this the chain is an unreadable wall of numbers.

exit_check.prompt: State what a European call gives its holder the right to do, and name the four contract terms that fully specify it.
rubric: states a right to buy at the strike on expiry, not an obligation
names underlying, strike, expiry and option type
distinguishes the buyer's position from the writer's

known_pitfalls.symptom: confuses the option premium with the strike
known_pitfalls.cause: both are prices, but one is paid now and one is the exercise level

nodes.title: Payoff and moneyness
nodes.why: You need the payoff line before a theoretical price means anything to you.

exit_check.prompt: For a call struck at 100, compute the expiry payoff at spot 80, 100 and 120, and sketch the payoff line.
rubric: payoffs computed as max(S-K, 0), giving 0, 0 and 20
sketch is flat below the strike and rises at 45 degrees above it
marks break-even at strike plus premium, not at the strike

known_pitfalls.symptom: draws break-even at the strike
known_pitfalls.cause: the premium paid up front is left out of the payoff

nodes.title: Black-Scholes inputs and assumptions
nodes.why: The final node of this graph asks you where the model breaks. This is where you find out what it assumed.

exit_check.prompt: List the five inputs to Black-Scholes and name two assumptions the model makes that real markets violate.
rubric: names spot, strike, time to expiry, risk-free rate and volatility
names constant volatility as an assumption markets violate
names lognormal returns or costless continuous hedging as a second violated assumption

known_pitfalls.symptom: counts the option price as a sixth input
known_pitfalls.cause: price is the output; it becomes an input only when solving for implied volatility

nodes.title: Implement Black-Scholes in Python
nodes.why: This function is the engine the whole pipeline exists to run.

exit_check.prompt: Write bs_price(S, K, T, r, sigma, kind) and match a reference implementation to four decimals on ten random inputs.
rubric: d1 and d2 are computed correctly
call and put branches are both implemented
output matches a reference to 4 decimals on 10 random inputs
returns intrinsic value at T=0 instead of raising

known_pitfalls.symptom: put prices come out negative
known_pitfalls.cause: sign error in put-call parity, or N(-d) written as -N(d)

known_pitfalls.symptom: division by zero at expiry
known_pitfalls.cause: sigma * sqrt(T) is a denominator and T reaches 0

nodes.title: Delta and vega
nodes.why: Vega is the derivative your implied-volatility solver needs, so this is a prerequisite disguised as a side quest.

exit_check.prompt: Return delta and vega analytically from your pricer, then verify both against a finite-difference approximation.
rubric: delta returns N(d1) for a call
vega is identical for a call and a put at the same strike
analytic values match finite differences to 3 decimals

known_pitfalls.symptom: vega is out by a factor of 100
known_pitfalls.cause: vega per one volatility point versus per unit of volatility

nodes.title: Implied volatility by Newton-Raphson
nodes.why: Market quotes carry a price, not a volatility. Inverting the model is how you compare like with like.

exit_check.prompt: Solve for implied volatility using your vega, and recover sigma from a price your own pricer produced.
rubric: iterates using vega rather than bisecting blindly
recovers the input sigma to 4 decimals on a round trip
caps iterations and returns NaN instead of looping forever on non-convergence

known_pitfalls.symptom: solver diverges on deep out-of-the-money contracts
known_pitfalls.cause: vega approaches zero there, so the Newton step explodes

nodes.title: Tradier sandbox auth and a first quote
nodes.why: Cheapest possible proof that you can reach the data at all, before any Spark exists.

exit_check.prompt: Get a Tradier sandbox token and pull a single equity quote from the command line.
rubric: token is read from an environment variable rather than pasted into the source
a quote request returns HTTP 200 with a parseable body
prints the last traded price for one symbol

known_pitfalls.symptom: 401 despite a valid-looking token
known_pitfalls.cause: sandbox and production tokens are not interchangeable across hosts

nodes.title: Pull a full option chain
nodes.why: The chain is the actual shape of your input data, and it is much wider than a quote.

exit_check.prompt: Pull a full option chain for one underlying and one expiry, then count the contracts returned.
rubric: the request carries an expiration parameter
the response is parsed into rows carrying strike, bid, ask and option type
the row count equals the number of strikes times two

known_pitfalls.symptom: only calls come back
known_pitfalls.cause: the chain endpoint was filtered by option type without noticing

nodes.title: Rate limits and backoff
nodes.why: Polling a chain every few seconds hits the limit within a session, and a dead poller silently starves the stream.

exit_check.prompt: Make your client survive a 429 by backing off, and show the retry succeeding in a log.
rubric: reads the rate-limit headers on each response
backs off exponentially with jitter rather than sleeping a fixed interval
a log shows a 429 followed by a successful retry

known_pitfalls.symptom: retries stampede after an outage
known_pitfalls.cause: fixed backoff without jitter synchronises every client

nodes.title: Spark DataFrame basics
nodes.why: Everything downstream is a DataFrame operation; streaming only changes where the rows come from.

exit_check.prompt: Load a CSV of option quotes, filter to one expiry, and aggregate contract counts by strike.
rubric: the schema is declared explicitly rather than inferred
filter and groupBy produce the expected row count
explain() output is pasted, showing the physical plan

known_pitfalls.symptom: schema inference silently types strikes as strings
known_pitfalls.cause: inferSchema on mixed CSV columns falls back to string

nodes.title: readStream and writeStream
nodes.why: This is the smallest thing that is genuinely a stream rather than a loop around a batch job.

exit_check.prompt: Turn your CSV load into a file-source stream that writes counts to the console sink.
rubric: readStream declares a schema, which the file source requires
writeStream uses an output mode valid for the aggregation
console output updates when a new file lands in the source directory

known_pitfalls.symptom: append mode rejected on an aggregation
known_pitfalls.cause: append needs a watermark before an aggregate output is final

nodes.title: Checkpointing and exactly-once restart
nodes.why: A pricing job that double-counts ticks after a restart produces numbers nobody can trust.

exit_check.prompt: Kill your stream mid-batch, restart it, and show that no rows were duplicated.
rubric: checkpointLocation is configured on the writer
the restart resumes from the committed offset rather than from the start
the output row count matches the single-run baseline

known_pitfalls.symptom: the stream will not restart after a code change
known_pitfalls.cause: the checkpoint holds a query plan and schema that no longer match

known_pitfalls.symptom: rows reappear after a restart
known_pitfalls.cause: the sink is not idempotent, so at-least-once delivery shows up as duplicates

nodes.title: Recover an incompatible checkpoint
nodes.why: Your restart failed on a checkpoint incompatibility, not on the streaming logic itself.
nodes.diagnosis: The stream refuses to restart after a code change because the checkpoint stores a query plan and state schema that no longer match the modified job.
remediation: read the exception and identify whether offsets, state or schema is the incompatible part
run the modified query against a fresh checkpoint directory to confirm the new code is otherwise sound
choose deliberately between discarding accumulated state and reshaping the change to stay compatible

exit_check.prompt: Change your aggregation, trigger the restart failure on purpose, then restart cleanly and name what caused it.
rubric: reproduces the incompatibility deliberately rather than stumbling into it
names offsets, state or schema as the specific incompatible part
restarts successfully and states what was given up to do so

nodes.title: Event time and watermarks
nodes.why: Quotes arrive out of order. Without a watermark the job holds state forever and eventually dies.

exit_check.prompt: Add event-time windowing with a watermark, then feed a deliberately late record and show it dropped.
rubric: withWatermark is applied to the event-time column before the aggregation
a record later than the threshold is absent from the output
the same record inside the threshold does appear in the output

known_pitfalls.symptom: state grows without bound
known_pitfalls.cause: the aggregation keys on a column that is not bounded by the watermark

nodes.title: Vectorized pandas UDFs
nodes.why: Black-Scholes row by row in a Python UDF is slow enough to stall the stream; vectorizing is what makes it viable.

exit_check.prompt: Rewrite a scalar Python UDF as a pandas UDF and measure the speedup over 100k rows.
rubric: the function is annotated with a pandas UDF type and a return type
it operates on a Series rather than one scalar per row
wall-clock timings for both versions are reported

known_pitfalls.symptom: pandas UDF is slower than the scalar version
known_pitfalls.cause: the batch size is tiny, so Arrow serialisation dominates

nodes.title: Build the ingestion layer
nodes.why: This is where the API half and the Spark half first have to survive each other.

exit_check.prompt: Poll the chain on a schedule, land the raw responses, and expose them to Spark as a stream.
rubric: raw responses are landed before any parsing, so a bad parse stays replayable
malformed payloads are routed aside rather than killing the job
the stream emits rows across at least two consecutive polls

known_pitfalls.symptom: the job dies on one bad payload
known_pitfalls.cause: parsing happens inline with ingestion, so there is nothing to replay

nodes.title: Black-Scholes as a streaming UDF
nodes.why: The moment the finance half and the Spark half become one program.

exit_check.prompt: Apply your pricer to the streaming chain as a pandas UDF and emit a theoretical price per contract.
rubric: the pricer runs vectorized over a Series rather than row by row
time to expiry is derived from the quote timestamp, not from wall-clock now()
output carries the theoretical price alongside the market mid

known_pitfalls.symptom: every contract prices as worthless near the close
known_pitfalls.cause: time to expiry computed in the wrong unit, so T collapses to zero

nodes.title: End-to-end priced chain for one session
nodes.why: The goal, stated as something you either produced or did not.

exit_check.prompt: Run the whole pipeline for one market session and produce a table of market mid against your theoretical price.
rubric: the pipeline runs unattended for a full session with no manual restart
the output table covers at least fifty contracts
a restart mid-session leaves no duplicate rows

known_pitfalls.symptom: gaps in the output around the open
known_pitfalls.cause: the poller starts before the chain is populated and never backfills

nodes.title: Where the model breaks
nodes.why: A pipeline that prices contracts without telling you when to distrust it is worse than no pipeline.

exit_check.prompt: Pick the five contracts where your price diverged most from the market mid, and account for each divergence.
rubric: names the volatility smile as a source of divergence away from the money
separates model error from data error such as a stale or very wide quote
states one condition under which the divergence would be arbitrage rather than model error

known_pitfalls.symptom: blames the data for every divergence
known_pitfalls.cause: a single flat volatility input guarantees a smile-shaped error pattern

events.detail: restart raised an incompatibility after the aggregation was changed
recovery materialized from the failure on n_checkpointing

mutations.reason: Diagnostic answers located the failure in checkpoint compatibility rather than in the streaming logic, so the gap is local to this unit and does not need a new prerequisite.
